title: FBI SL 11.9.26

communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

You are receiving this correspondence as a request under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. subsection 552. I am requesting the following:

Copies of all Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) records, documents, and communications responsive to Salvatore LaRussa, aka Sam the Barber (April 6, 1938 - August 18, 1996; SSN 173-28-0732).

Mr. LaRussa was a restaurateur and associate of the Bruno crime family in Philadelphia. He was born in Campo dell Gatto, Italy, to Giuseppe (Joseph) LaRussa and Marianna LaRussa in 1938 and moved to the United States in 1951. A decade later, he began running so-called bust-out bars for the Bruno crime family in Philadelphia's red-light district on Locust Street, including the Bag o' Nails and HMS Pinafore; these were Mob-run dives that offered nude dancers and prostitution. The businesses provided Mr. LaRussa with enough capital to open a restaurant, La Cucina, that quickly became a hangout for Nicodemo "Little Nicky" Scarfo, successor to Bruno family boss Angelo Bruno. Mr. Scarfo would later use Mr. LaRussa's home in Whitemarsh Township, PA as the site for initiation ceremonies for his criminal organization.

Mr. LaRussa died on August, 18, 1996, and his grave is listed publicly on Find A Grave: https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/123805574/salvatore-la_russa

I have also attached a copy of his obituary from the August 21, 1996 edition of The Philadelphia Inquirer.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Records System, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for Mr. LaRussa under his name and all-known aliases related to Angelo Bruno, Nicodemo Scarfo, A. Charles Peruto, and Raymond Horsch.

In the event that there are fees, I am willing to pay up to $100. Please advise if fees will exceed this amount so I might make an arrangement for requesting the records. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

I look forward to your response within 20 working days, as the statute requires. If access to the records I am requesting will take longer, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption you feel justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law.

Sincerely,

Robert Skvarla, Jr.

I am requesting emails between your agency and LexisNexis Risk Solutions, and emails concerning LexisNexis Risk Solutions.

1) Domains: all emails between your agency and "@lexisnexis.com", "@lexisnexisrisk.com", or "@lnssi.com". Timeframe: June 15, 2026 through the date this request is completed.

3) Include: emails, attachments, inline and embedded images, links, and the subject and to/from/cc lines. Please provide the original emails in full.

4) Exclude: Duplicates and mass-mailings may be de-duplicated so that only a single representative example is produced. Some agencies receive an automated message every time a data upload to LexisNexis completes. At some departments that runs past 1,400 messages a month. We want to establish the frequency and see an example, not receive thousands of identical emails. Automated password reset and account notification emails may be excluded.

5) Format: if possible, please provide the original electronic files (.eml, .msg, .mbox, .pst, or a similar native format) so the integrity of the original messages is preserved. 

6) If any emails are withheld in whole or in part, please include a list of what was withheld and cite the specific exemption relied on for each.

7) If you coordinate or discuss the response to this request with LexisNexis in any way, please include the email, text message, meeting invite, or other media showing the conversation you had with LexisNexis relating to this request.
